niche.habitat: Surface wind-scoured dunes of magnetite sand and Fe-sulfide outcrops
niche.diet: Obligate consumer of magnetotactic bacterial mats; supplements with iron-oxidizing chemolithotrophs
niche.active: Diurnal crepuscular; avoids peak flare UV by retreating to burrows or using coil-shielding

body: Bronze-chitin carapace with four retractable helical coil-appendages along the dorsal flanks; eyes possess radical-pair aligned cryptochromes; gut packed with magnetosome chains

chains.trait: Bronzed helical coils modulate near-field dipole pulses
links: Coils generate modulated B-field for social signaling
Near-field dipole falls off as 1/r^3; range limited to 12 cm contact-adjacent

Why beats sound: Dense 2.6 bar atmosphere (F8) creates high acoustic impedance and wind-noise from shifting dunes; magnetic pulses are directional, immune to scattering, and require less energy than shouting in thick air
Why beats light: K-dwarf flares (F1) cause plasma ionization and auroral glare (F6) that washes out polarization cues; magnetic channel remains clear and safe from UV damage
Energy cost: 1.8 W peak for a 60 ms pulse; requires high-calorie bacterial diet

skill.effect: Establishes a private 12 cm magnetic channel with an ally; ally gains +25% stealth (immune to acoustic detection) and shares heat-dissipation cooldown for 4 turns.

chains.weakness: Eddy heating: If exposed to external alternating field >1 mT, coils overheat and the Cobrezo takes 1 damage/turn and cannot pulse for 2 turns.
observe: Dorsal coils twitch in rhythmic metallic clicks
Iron-dust on the sand clumps into fractal patterns near the creature
Skin shimmers with copper iridescence when excited

journal.en: It whispers to the metal in the wind; a silent language no predator can hear.

plausibility.summary: Cap pulse rate; tie 1.8 W to explicit body mass (~200–500 g) or to superconducting-like iron-core coils; keep range at contact–12 cm; frame as highly speculative convergent analog to electric-fish signaling, not a known terrestrial mechanism.
fixes: Cap pulse rate; tie 1.8 W to explicit body mass (~200–500 g) or to superconducting-like iron-core coils; keep range at contact–12 cm; frame as highly speculative convergent analog to electric-fish signaling, not a known terrestrial mechanism.

analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Symbionts provide stable internal reference for heading
Dietary iron sequestered in magnetosomes prevents Fe toxicity (F11)

Why beats alternatives: Radical-pair sensors (F12) are susceptible to local field anomalies from crustal deposits; bacterial chains average out noise, allowing reliable navigation through complex magnetite terrain
Evolutionary link: Symbiosis allows exploitation of iron-rich niche without oxidative stress

skill.effect: Consume magnetotactic bacteria; heal 2 HP and gain 'Magnetic Sense' (+1 to identify magnetic anomalies) for 3 turns.

chains.weakness: Iron toxicity threshold: If environment exceeds 5 mM free Fe ions (F11), the symbionts die, causing -2 Will and vulnerability to magnetic disruption.
observe: Gut region glows faintly with aligned chains when resting
Creature scratches its shell against magnetite rocks to feed symbionts
Compass spins wildly near pure magnetite outcrops

journal.en: Its stomach holds a compass of living iron.

plausibility.summary: Internal magnetite chains can supply a stable reference axis that filters local crustal noise on radical-pair heading sensors (F12, F13), and sequestering dietary iron fits Fe toxicity zoning (F11) on magnetite dunes (F10). Gut or pouched magnetotactic symbionts are not a classic Earth headline mutualism, but magnetosome biomineralization and host-associated magnetotactic lineages are real; calibration-by-symbiont is speculative but selection on an iron-obligate forager in a high-field world is coherent.
fixes: Internal magnetite chains can supply a stable reference axis that filters local crustal noise on radical-pair heading sensors (F12, F13), and sequestering dietary iron fits Fe toxicity zoning (F11) on magnetite dunes (F10). links: Creature curls coils into a Faraday cage around sensory organs
Protection against ionizing radiation and induced currents
Driven by frequent energetic UV/X-ray flares (F1) and auroral precipitation
Behavioral adaptation to young K-dwarf activity without requiring full armor mass

skill.effect: Enter defensive posture; negate all radiation damage and magnetic disruption effects for 3 turns, but movement speed halved.

chains.weakness: During the hunker, the Cobrezo cannot act and is vulnerable to grapple.
observe: Coils snap shut into a bronze sphere
Creature buries legs in sand, exposing only shielded eyes
Aura flickers as static charge dissipates

journal.en: When the sky screams, it becomes a statue of safety.

plausibility.summary: Storm Hunker: negate magnetic disruption and induced eddy damage; partial UV reduction only when buried; full flare/belt mitigation stays tied to F17 symbionts/repair, not the coil sphere alone.
fixes: Storm Hunker: negate magnetic disruption and induced eddy damage; partial UV reduction only when buried; full flare/belt mitigation stays tied to F17 symbionts/repair, not the coil sphere alone.

chains.trait: Radial-pair cryptochromes aligned to magnetic inclination
links: Eyes contain flavin-tryptophan radical pairs sensitive to field vector
Allows detection of magnetic anomalies and inclination gradients
Useful for navigating along crustal anomaly corridors (F18)
Convergent with F12; provides 'magnetic vision' overlay in the copper sky

skill.effect: Perceive magnetic field lines as a visual overlay; reveals hidden corridors, magnetic traps, and weak points in magnetic shielding (+2 to interact with magnetic mechanics).

chains.weakness: Disorientation: Sudden changes in field intensity (>20% jump) cause stun for 1 turn as radical-pair yields scramble.
observe: Eyes track invisible gradients, tilting head to measure inclination
Vision seems to double when magnetic activity is high
Retinal glow matches the copper sky polarization

journal.en: It sees the invisible rivers of the world.

relations.note: Ostracilo evolved analogous coil-structures in a conductive medium; Cobrezo coils are air-optimized, Ostracilo coils are induction-optimized.
Both use magnetic comms but in different media; Cobrezo uses air for directional pulses, Ostracilo uses induction for contact stealth.

body_plan.origin: Surface-dwelling arthropod-analogue diverging from a burrowing ancestor

temperament: Highly cooperative, skittish to acoustic surprise, responsive to magnetic 'touch'
secrets: Coil-reversal: By momentarily reversing polarity, a Cobrezo can induce a mild tetany in a rival's muscles, stunning them at contact range.
Dietary secret: The creature can voluntarily shed its symbiont chain to become magnetically invisible to predators that track magnetic signatures, but loses compass ability.
moments: A storm of iron-sand rises, blinding the herd. The Cobrezo leader locks coils, and instantly every individual in the dune halts, their breath syncing to the magnetic pulse, moving as a single bronze ghost through the gale.

journal.en: They do not speak; they resonate.
The wind carries noise, but the field carries truth.
